This article argues that these changes contributed to delayed detection in the 2026 Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda, declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) by WHO on May 17. While the concurrent Andes hantavirus cluster linked to a cruise ship is less directly tied to field surveillance losses, both events highlight vulnerabilities in early warning and international coordination. Fiscal restraint is a legitimate policy aim, yet evidence suggests that abrupt termination of proven surveillance systems has impaired timely responses to inevitable threats, with implications for global security.
